thread.document:
Working with Claude Opus 4.5 on implementing SSM (State Space Model) forward passes, I explored both recurrence-based and convolution-based approaches, including optimizations for diagonal weight matrices. The interaction demonstrated strong coding capabilities but revealed some notable patterns in how the model handles complexity analysis and debugging.

One-shot successes:

Core implementation logic for all four functions (unrolled, convolution, diagonal variants)

Divide-and-conquer kernel construction algorithm

Required correction/hints:

Data type mismatch: Initially used NumPy arrays (np.zeros) instead of PyTorch tensors, causing a TypeError when mixed with tensor inputs. Fixed immediately after providing the error message.

Complexity analysis: Initially overcomplicated the convolution runtime analysis, including unnecessary terms. Required a hint to focus on the dominant cost from make_conv_kernel and properly analyze the divide-and-conquer recurrence to arrive at O(TH3).

Scope clarification: Needed reminding to focus only on T and H (not N and D) for complexity analysis.

Strengths observed:

Good intuition about parallelism vs. computational complexity trade-offs on CPU vs GPU

Quickly adapted when given corrective feedback

Areas requiring guidance:

Tendency to over-specify complexity bounds before simplifying

Didn't initially catch the NumPy/PyTorch inconsistency despite the context being clearly PyTorch-based
